Left-hander Lee Seung-hyun steps in for FedEx, who is out with a "throat issue," but collapses after surviving the first inning, allowing three home runs… A rough outing of 5 earned runs over 4 innings

Updated:2026.10.04 ・ 15:49

박수진
Add as preferred source

*This content was translated by AI.

He could not bear the weight of a sudden start. Samsung Lions left-handed pitcher Lee Seung-hyun (24), who took the mound in place of foreign pitcher Chris FedEx, who was sidelined due to a "throat issue," allowed three home runs and finished with 5 earned runs over 4 innings, leaving a sense of regret.

Lee started the home game against the Doosan Bears at Daegu Samsung Lions Park on the 4th, throwing 68 pitches over 4 innings while allowing 5 runs. According to the pitching analysis sheet provided by the Samsung club, he mixed in a two-seam fastball with a top speed of 144 km/h, along with curves and sliders, but failed to suppress the long balls from Doosan batters at every critical moment.

FedEx, who was originally scheduled to start on this day, complained of a throat issue before the game and could not take the field. As a result, left-hander Lee Seung-hyun was rushed in as the replacement starter.

Lee's start was relatively stable on this day. In the top of the first inning, he gave up a leadoff single to Park Chan-ho, but induced consecutive infield grounders from the following An Jae-seok and Park Jun-soon, retiring the runners in order. He then recorded a foul fly out by shortstop against No. 4 hitter Yang Eui-ji in just four pitches, completing a scoreless inning with only nine balls thrown.

However, he began to waver under the firepower of the Doosan lineup from the top of the second inning. He allowed a solo home run to left field off the bat of leadoff batter Severino on the fifth pitch of a 2-2 count, carrying a distance of 115 meters. Following a single by Kim Min-seok and an infield hit by Jeong Soobin, he found himself in a bases-loaded situation with two outs and runners on first and second base, but ended the inning without further damage by striking out Kim Dae-han in three pitches and getting Park Chan-ho to ground into short. He threw 26 pitches in the second inning alone, causing his pitch count to surge rapidly.

He could not get through the hurdle of the top of the third inning. After allowing a double to center field by leadoff batter An Jae-seok, a wild pitch compounded the trouble, putting him in a bases-loaded situation with no outs. He then recorded his second run allowed on an infield hit to shortstop by Park Jun-soon. Next, he was punished for a two-run home run to left field (distance 110 meters) off No. 4 hitter Yang Eui-ji's bat on the second pitch, and the score instantly widened to 0-4. He struck out Severino and retired Kim Min-seok with an outfield fly ball after a seven-pitch at-bat, but then surrendered another solo home run to left field (distance 115 meters) to No. 7 hitter Yang Seok-hwan on the first pitch, giving up four runs in the third inning alone.

In the top of the fourth inning, he gave up a single to left field to Park Chan-ho after one out but did not allow any runs. Lee's final line for the day was 4 innings, 9 hits allowed (3 home runs), 3 strikeouts, and 5 earned runs. He was replaced by Im Ki-young at the start of the top of the fifth inning, ending his appearance, but he collapsed under the barrage of three Doosan home runs that erupted consecutively in the second and third innings, swallowing his regret as a replacement starter.
